import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffBaseChange
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyPullbackGlued

/-!
# Certified base change on the widened cover (R2, human decision I-0492)

The seven certificate clauses of `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` transport along an arbitrary test
change `R → R'`.  This is the last structural piece the widened value needed: without it
`DivFamZarAff` is a type with no functoriality, and nothing downstream can base-change a
widened class.

## Two definitional identities do most of the work

Both were probed and hold on the nose, which is why this file is short:

* the base-changed overlap **is** the preimage of the overlap
  (`(D.baseChange R').pieces i ⊓ (D.baseChange R').pieces j = relCurveMap ⁻¹ᵁ (pieces i ⊓
  pieces j)` by `rfl`, since `⁻¹ᵁ` commutes with `⊓` definitionally on `Opens`);
* the pulled colength **is** the quotient `relQuotBaseChangeAff` lands in.

So the widened colength and overlap transports are the SAME declaration
(`AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange`) at two different opens, where the chart-typed layer
needed `pieceQuotBaseChange` and a separately-constructed `ovlQuotBaseChange` conjugated
through the overlap generator.

## What is reused verbatim

Clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) ride the abstract `FlatCokernel` keystones
(`LinearMap.ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker`, `LinearMap.tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker`,
`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`) and the two square-transport lemmas
(`LinearEquiv.map_ker_of_comp_eq`, `LinearEquiv.range_eq_map_range_of_comp_eq`).  All are
stated for bare modules and know nothing about covers, so the widening does not touch them.

## Main declarations

* `AffAdaptation.colengthBaseChange`, `ovlColengthBaseChange` — the (c1) and overlap
  transports, both `AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange`.
* `AffAdaptation.chartProdBaseChange`, `ovlProdBaseChange` — the product transports.
* `AffAdaptation.delta_baseChange_comm` — `δ`-naturality, a `funext` over the pair index.
* `AffAdaptation.gluedBaseChange` and the (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transports.
* `AffAdaptation.isCertified_pullback` — **the certificate base-changes**, all seven clauses.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TopologicalSpace
open Opposite TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']

namespace AffAdaptation

variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : AffAdaptation D d) (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))

/-! ## The colength transports (clause (c1)) -/

/-- **Base change of a piece colength**: `R' ⊗[R] colength j ≃ₐ[R'] (pullback).colength j`.
This is `AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange` at the singleton `{eqn j}`; the target is
definitionally the pulled colength. -/
noncomputable def colengthBaseChange (j : D.index) :
    R' ⊗[R] A.colength j ≃ₐ[R'] (A.pullback R' hproj).colength j :=
  (D.pieceQuotBaseChange R' j {A.eqn j}).trans
    (Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq R' (by rw [Set.image_singleton]; rfl))

/-- (c1) transport, finiteness. -/
theorem finite_colength_pullback (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)) (j : D.index) :
    Module.Finite R' ((A.pullback R' hproj).colength j) := by
  haveI := hfin j
  exact Module.Finite.equiv (A.colengthBaseChange R' hproj j).toLinearEquiv

/-- (c1) transport, projectivity. -/
theorem projective_colength_pullback (j : D.index) :
    Module.Projective R' ((A.pullback R' hproj).colength j) := by
  haveI := hproj j
  exact Module.Projective.of_equiv (A.colengthBaseChange R' hproj j).toLinearEquiv

/-- **Base change of an overlap colength**.  The SAME declaration as the piece transport, at
the open `pieces i ⊓ pieces j` — no overlap generator, no conjugation.  Requires the overlap
to be affine, which is a hypothesis rather than a field: `AffCoverData` demands affineness of
the pieces only, and overlaps are affine when the relative curve is separated. -/
noncomputable def ovlColengthBaseChange
    (hinf : ∀ i j : D.index, IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) (i j : D.index) :
    R' ⊗[R] A.ovlColength i j ≃ₐ[R'] (A.pullback R' hproj).ovlColength i j :=
  (relQuotBaseChangeAff C R' (hinf i j)
      {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
       relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}).trans
    (Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq R' (by
      rw [Set.image_insert_eq, Set.image_singleton]
      exact congrArg₂ (fun x y => Ideal.span {x, y})
        (relAffSectionsMap_res C R'
          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)).symm
        (relAffSectionsMap_res C R'
          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)).symm))

/-! ## The computation rules of the two transports -/

lemma colengthBaseChange_one_tmul_mk (j : D.index) (t : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)) :
    A.colengthBaseChange R' hproj j
        ((1 : R') ⊗ₜ[R] Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) t) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(A.pullback R' hproj).eqn j})
        (D.piecesMap R' j t) := by
  rw [colengthBaseChange, AlgEquiv.trans_apply,
    AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange_one_tmul_mk, Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq_mk]

lemma ovlColengthBaseChange_one_tmul_mk
    (hinf : ∀ i j : D.index, IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) (i j : D.index)
    (t : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) :
    A.ovlColengthBaseChange R' hproj hinf i j
        ((1 : R') ⊗ₜ[R] Ideal.Quotient.mk (A.ovlIdeal i j) t) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk ((A.pullback R' hproj).ovlIdeal i j)
        (relAffSectionsMap C R' (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) t) := by
  rw [ovlColengthBaseChange, AlgEquiv.trans_apply, relQuotBaseChangeAff_one_tmul_mk]
  exact Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq_mk R' _ _

structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
  m₀ : ℕ
  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
  m₁ : ℕ
  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1

namespace FinCoverData

variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)

/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m₀ ⊕ Fin D.m₁

/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))

@[simp]
lemma pieces_inl (j : Fin D.m₀) :
    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma pieces_inr (j : Fin D.m₁) :
    D.pieces (Sum.inr j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) := rfl

/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴿ`. -/
lemma cover₀ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ≤
    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₀, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) :=
  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₀ D.h₀ D.partition₀

/-- The chart-1 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₁ᴿ`. -/
lemma cover₁ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤
    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₁, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) :=
  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₁ D.h₁ D.partition₁

end FinCoverData

/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (fun c x => by
      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
      rw [map_mul]
      congr 1
      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)

@[simp]
lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
  rfl

/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
  toFinCoverData := D
  eqn := eqn
  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl

/-!
# The native module carried by a glued rank-one datum

`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` is already a sheaf of modules over the coefficient
ring.  The presentation contract also asks for the same object as a sheaf of
modules over the structure sheaf of the relative curve.  This file supplies
that bridge: the componentwise `gluedQsmul` action gives a module on every open,
`gluedRes_gluedQsmul` gives the semilinearity needed by
`PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf`, and `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies its
restriction to the coefficient ring with the original datum sheaf.

The canonical piece trivializations also prove that the native module is a line
bundle.  Pushforward base-change and existence of a tied
`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` remain genuine producer obligations.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

noncomputable section

variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)

/-- The structure-sheaf module on the sections of the glued datum over one open.

The action is the componentwise multiplication action; the four module laws
are inherited from the corresponding `gluedQsmul` identities. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleOn (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
      ((D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)).obj (op U)) := by
  change Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U))
  letI : SMul Γ(relCurve C B, U)
      (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U)) :=
    ⟨fun r s => gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s⟩
  exact Module.ofMinimalAxioms
    (fun r x y => gluedQsmul_add B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x y)
    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_add_left B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_mul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    (fun x => gluedQsmul_one B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) x)

/-- The presheaf of structure-sheaf modules underlying `D`. -/
noncomputable def nativePresheaf : (relCurve C B).PresheafOfModules := by
  let M : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)
  let family : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) :=
    fun U => moduleOn D U.unop
  letI : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) := family
  exact PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf M (by
    intro X Y f r m
    change gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le
        (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : X.unop ≤ X.unop) r m) =
      gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : Y.unop ≤ Y.unop)
        ((relCurve C B).resHom f.unop.le r)
        (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le m)
    rw [gluedRes_gluedQsmul]
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext j
    rw [gluedQsmul_coe, gluedQsmul_coe]
    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom])

/-- The native `Scheme.Modules` object associated to a glued datum. -/
noncomputable def nativeModule : (relCurve C B).Modules := by
  refine ⟨nativePresheaf D, ?_⟩
  rw [show (nativePresheaf D).presheaf =
    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat) from rfl]
  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} B))).mp D.sheaf.property using 1
  all_goals rfl

/-! ## Piecewise line-bundle trivializations -/

/-- Sections of the native module over one cocycle piece are the structure-ring sections.

The open-immersion ring equivalence transports the component trivialization from the ambient
relative curve to the restricted scheme.  The `gluedTriv_gluedQsmul` identity is exactly the
structure-sheaf semilinearity needed for this to be a linear equivalence over the restricted
ring of sections. -/
noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv
    (j : D.index) (V : (D.pieces j).toScheme.Opens) :
    Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) ≃ₗ[
      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) := by
  let e := gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
  let ρ := ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
  let f : Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) →ₗ[
      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) :=
    { toFun := fun s => ρ (e s)
      map_add' := by
        intro s t
        change ρ (e (s + t)) = ρ (e s) + ρ (e t)
        change ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t)) =
          ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s) +
            ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t)
        rw [show gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t) =
            gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s +
              gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t by
              exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).map_add s t]
        exact ρ.map_add _ _
      map_smul' := by
        intro r s
        change ρ
            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
              (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl) (ρ.symm r) s)) =
          r * ρ
            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s)
        rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul]
        simp [ρ] }
  apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective f
  constructor
  · intro s t h
    have h' := congrArg ρ.symm h
    dsimp [f] at h'
    rw [ρ.symm_apply_apply, ρ.symm_apply_apply] at h'
    exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).injective h'
  · intro r
    refine ⟨e.symm (ρ.symm r), ?_⟩
    change ρ (e (e.symm (ρ.symm r))) = r
    rw [e.apply_symm_apply, ρ.apply_symm_apply]

/-- The piecewise section equivalences assemble to a sheaf isomorphism with the unit module. -/
noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSheafIso (j : D.index) :
    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D) ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit (D.pieces j).toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
  (SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _).preimageIso
    (PresheafOfModules.isoMk
      (fun V => (nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv D j V.unop).toModuleIso)
      (fun {V W} f => by
        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro x
        change
          ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso W.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le W.unop)
                (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit
                  ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop)) x)) =
            (D.pieces j).toScheme.presheaf.map f
              (((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
                (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x))
        rw [gluedTriv_res B D.isGluingCocycle j
          ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
          ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x]
        simp only [Scheme.Opens.ι_appIso]
        change
          (relCurve C B).resHom
              ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x) =
            (relCurve C B).presheaf.map
              ((D.pieces j).ι.opensFunctor.map f.unop).op
              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x)
        rfl))

/-- The canonical native module is locally a free rank-one structure-sheaf module. -/
theorem nativeModule_isLineBundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle (nativeModule D) := by
  intro x
  let j := D.pieceIndex x
  refine ⟨D.pieces j, D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex x, ?_⟩
  exact ⟨nativeModulePieceSheafIso D j⟩

/-- On every open, restricting `D.nativeModule` to the coefficient ring recovers
the datum's original module of sections.

The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive
point: `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies the native structure-sheaf action
of a coefficient scalar with the datum's coefficient action. -/
noncomputable def nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv
    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) ≃ₗ[B]
      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by
  let f :
      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
        (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[B]
        D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) :=
    { toFun := fun x => x
      map_add' := by
        intros
        rfl
      map_smul' := by
        intro r x
        change gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U)
            ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B U r) x =
          r • (show D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) from x)
        exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap B D.pieces D.unit
          (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x }
  exact LinearEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun y => ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.

This has exactly the type of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.module_iso` when the
presentation's native module is chosen to be `D.nativeModule`. -/
noncomputable def nativeModuleKSheafIso :
    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D) ≅ D.sheaf :=
  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimageIso
    (NatIso.ofComponents
      (fun U => (nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv D U.unop).toModuleIso)
      (fun {_ _} _ => by
        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro x
        rfl))

end

end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

end AlgebraicGeometry

refine ⟨D.pieces j, D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex x, ?_⟩
  exact ⟨nativeModulePieceSheafIso D j⟩

The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive

      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by

/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafDatum

/-!
# Base change of the pinned cocycle datum (DAT-1, stage 1d-ii, the datum half)

The `relCocycleBaseChange`-style base change of the basic-open cocycle datum
(`informal/spec-dat-1.md` stage (1d-ii), first bullet; worksheet §3.2 — **this is the
RE-5 transport interface**): along a `k`-algebra map `B → B'`, the generators, partition
coefficients and transition units of a `Scheme.BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` push forward
through the relative-curve comparison morphism `relCurveMap C B B'` to a datum over `B'`,
with the pieces mapping to pieces (`Scheme.preimage_basicOpen`) and the partition/cocycle
identities carried by `map_*`.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appLE_resHom` — `appLE` commutes with restriction on
  both sides (the workhorse; both sides collapse to one `appLE` by
  `appLE_map`/`map_appLE` and proof irrelevance).
* `relSectionsMap_basicOpen` — basic opens of compared sections are preimages of basic
  opens.
* `relCurveMap_appLE_overAlgebraMap` — the comparison intertwines the structure algebra
  maps along `algebraMap B B'`, over **arbitrary** opens (the pullback-open case is the
  landed `relSectionsMap_overAlgebraMap`).
* `BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange` / `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.baseChange` — the datum base
  change, with `pieces_baseChange` (pieces map to pieces).
* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionsMap` — the componentwise comparison of glued sections
  `F_D(W) → F_{D'}(W')` for `W' ≤ relCurveMap ⁻¹ᵁ W`, additive
  (`sectionsMap_add`), semilinear along `algebraMap B B'` (`sectionsMap_smul`),
  commuting with restriction (`gluedRes_sectionsMap`), intertwining the piece
  trivializations with the section comparison (`gluedTriv_sectionsMap`) and the
  componentwise chart actions (`sectionsMap_gluedQsmul`) — the inputs of the stage
  (1d-ii) term identifications and the RE-5 transport.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

/-! ## `appLE` against restriction, on arbitrary opens -/

/-- **`appLE` commutes with restriction**: for `f : X ⟶ Y`, restricting the `appLE`
image of a section equals the `appLE` image of the restricted section. Both sides are
`f.appLE W PW'` of the section, by `appLE_map`/`map_appLE` and proof irrelevance of the
inclusion witnesses. -/
lemma Scheme.Hom.appLE_resHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X.Hom Y) {W' W : Y.Opens}
    {PW' PW : X.Opens} (hW : W' ≤ W) (ePW : PW ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W) (ePW' : PW' ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W')
    (hP : PW' ≤ PW) (s : Γ(Y, W)) :
    X.resHom hP ((f.appLE W PW ePW).hom s) =
      (f.appLE W' PW' ePW').hom (Y.resHom hW s) := by
  have h1 := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom
    $(Scheme.Hom.appLE_map f ePW (homOfLE hP).op)) s)
  have h2 := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom
    $(Scheme.Hom.map_appLE f ePW' (homOfLE hW).op)) s)
  exact h1.trans h2.symm

/-! ## Basic opens of compared sections -/

/-- **Basic opens base-change to basic opens**: the basic open of the compared section
`relSectionsMap s` is the `relCurveMap`-preimage of the basic open of `s`. -/
theorem relSectionsMap_basicOpen (V : C.left.Opens)
    (s : Γ(relCurve C B, (fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)) :
    (relCurve C B').basicOpen (relSectionsMap C B B' V s) =
      relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((relCurve C B).basicOpen s) := by
  have happ : relSectionsMap C B B' V s =
      (relCurve C B').resHom
        (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm :
          (fst C (overSpec k B')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤
            relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
        (((relCurveMap C B B').app ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)).hom s) := by
    have h := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom
      $(Scheme.Hom.appLE_map (relCurveMap C B B')
        (le_refl (relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)))
        (homOfLE (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm)).op)) s)
    have h0 : ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
        (relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)) le_rfl).hom s =
        (((relCurveMap C B B').app ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)).hom s) :=
      congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom
        $(Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app (relCurveMap C B B')
          (U := (fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))) s)
    calc relSectionsMap C B B' V s
        = ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
            ((fst C (overSpec k B')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
            (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm)).hom s := rfl
      _ = (relCurve C B').resHom (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V).symm)
            (((relCurveMap C B B').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
              (relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k B)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
              le_rfl).hom s) := h.symm
      _ = _ := by rw [h0]
  rw [happ, Scheme.basicOpen_resHom,
    ← Scheme.preimage_basicOpen (relCurveMap C B B') s,
    ← relCurveMap_preimage C B B' V, ← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf]
  congr 1
  exact inf_eq_right.mpr ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le s)

/-! ## The comparison intertwines the structure algebra maps (arbitrary opens) -/

/-- `appLE` is invariant under an equality of morphisms. -/
private lemma appLE_congr_hom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (h : f = g) {U : Y.Opens}
    {W : X.Opens} (e : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    f.appLE U W e = g.appLE U W (h ▸ e) := by
  subst h; rfl

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule

/-- **The comparison intertwines the structure actions, on arbitrary opens**: the
`appLE` image of the structure pullback of `r : B` is the structure pullback of
`algebraMap B B' r` (the landed `relSectionsMap_overAlgebraMap` is the pullback-open
case `W = V_B`). -/
theorem relCurveMap_appLE_overAlgebraMap {W : (relCurve C B).Opens}
    {W' : (relCurve C B').Opens} (hle : W' ≤ relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ W) (r : B) :
    ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE W W' hle).hom
        ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B W r) =
      (relCurve C B').overAlgebraMap B' W' (algebraMap B B' r) := by
  have hmor : ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫
        (snd C (overSpec k B)).left.appLE ⊤ W
          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).ge)) ≫
      (relCurveMap C B B').appLE W W' hle =
      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B') ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B')).inv ≫
        (snd C (overSpec k B')).left.appLE ⊤ W'
          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B')).left).ge) := by
    have hnat : (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appTop =
        CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B') ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B')).inv := by
      rw [Iso.inv_comp_eq, ← Category.assoc,
        ← Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B')),
        Category.assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
    have hsplit : ((snd C (overSpec k B')).left ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appLE ⊤ W'
          ((relCurveMap_snd C B B') ▸
            hle.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono _ (le_top.trans
              (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).ge))) =
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appLE ⊤ ⊤
            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top _).ge ≫
          (snd C (overSpec k B')).left.appLE ⊤ W'
            (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B')).left).ge) :=
      (Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE _ _ _ _ _ _ _).symm
    have happ : (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appLE ⊤ ⊤
        (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top _).ge =
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B B'))).appTop :=
      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
    rw [Category.assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE,
      appLE_congr_hom (relCurveMap_snd C B B'), hsplit, happ, ← Category.assoc,
      hnat, Category.assoc]
  have hoam : (relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B W r =
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫
        (snd C (overSpec k B)).left.appLE ⊤ W
          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B)).left).ge)).hom
        r := rfl
  have hoam' : (relCurve C B').overAlgebraMap B' W' (algebraMap B B' r) =
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B')).inv ≫
        (snd C (overSpec k B')).left.appLE ⊤ W'
          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd C (overSpec k B')).left).ge)).hom
        (algebraMap B B' r) := rfl
  rw [hoam, hoam']
  exact congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $hmor) r)

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

      "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient \u27e8sorry\u27e9` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

      "body": "DUPLICATION, DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean: the headline \"the FIRST inhabitant of DivFamZar at ANY parameter\" is FALSE over a field, and the uniqueness proof re-derives what two landed quotient-level lemmas already give.\n\nINHABITATION WAS NOT FIRST. exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq (DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:143, the landed B-3 hsurj) at D = 0 gives a DivFam C K pi 0 with divFamDivisor = 0, hence DivFamZar C K pi 0 via toZar; divFamFieldEquiv.symm (0, le_rfl, by simp) gives the same class directly, and Quotient.out of it gives a CertifiedDivisorFamily C K pi 0. VERIFIED in a probe importing ONLY DivisorFamilyFieldSurj + DivSchemeAbel, no pic-c file, lake env lean EXIT=0. The correct claim is narrower and still worth having: trivZar is the first inhabitant at a GENERAL TEST RING R, where no field-surjectivity route applies.\n\nUNIQUENESS RE-DERIVES A LANDED LEMMA. presentationDivisor_eq_zero_of_isCertified_zero + divEq_of_isCertified_zero (:103, :114) work per-adaptation and then re-run divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq. But divFamDivisor_injective (DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean:177) is exactly that step already packaged at the QUOTIENT level, and DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean imports DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv directly. With zero_le_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyField.lean:165) and deg_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:376), both also in closure, the whole file's math is:\n  hx : divFamDivisor x = 0 := eq_zero_of_deg_le_zero K (zero_le_divFamDivisor x) (deg rewrite; norm_num)\n  same for y; exact divFamDivisor_injective (hx.trans hy.symm)\nVERIFIED at the file's exact import list minus DivisorFamilyDegreeZero, EXIT=0. Two of the three declarations in the \"Main declarations\" list are avoidable, and the docstring's \"in one line each\" argument describes the longer of two routes without noting the shorter one exists.\n\nALSO: instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero and uniqueZeroOfField carry [LocallyOfFiniteType (relCurve C K over Spec K)] which is NOT load-bearing: it is inferInstance from the SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 binder two lines up (Smooth => LocallyOfFiniteType). Verified by re-elaborating both without it, EXIT=0.",

      "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP. I named ring-level surjectivity of  as the next brick; the actually-open statement is surjectivity of relPicToPicEt onto picEt -- a different map, different proof, and one the tree already treats as a real condition (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls membership in its range 'honesty'). A misidentified next brick sends the next lane to build something nobody needs.",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",
